purpose: Neutral cross-language golden vectors for AnchorReceipt transactions. Pins the SCALE signing bytes, the transaction signature, the full encoding, the transaction hash, and the serialised Transaction JSON object.

authority.receipt: test-vectors/receipt/receipt-v1.json — the receipt source of truth, referenced and never duplicated

conventions.hex: lowercase, no 0x prefix, except inside serialized_transaction which reproduces the JSON wire form
conventions.byte_order: fixed-width integers are little-endian and never compact
conventions.receipt_reference: receipt_vector names a vector in test-vectors/receipt/receipt-v1.json; resolve it there
conventions.sender: <receipt.executor> means: resolve the referenced receipt vector and use its executor, which consensus requires

derivation.method: Every expected value was constructed from the protocol rules, not by encoding with production Rust. SCALE laid out by hand as concatenated fields; integers by explicit fixed-width little-endian construction; signatures by an independent Ed25519; hashes by an independent BLAKE3. Rust is a consumer that must agree with values it did not produce.
derivation.upstream_truth: test-vectors/receipt/receipt-v1.json is the only machine input.

signing_formula.transaction_signing_payload: 0x03 || sender[32] || receiver[32] || amount_u128_le[16] || nonce_u64_le[8] || 0x01 || <full canonical receipt bytes>
signing_formula.transaction_hash: BLAKE3(full transaction), so it covers the signature
signing_formula.prehash: none — the transaction signature is over the raw signing payload bytes

discriminants.note: Both come from explicit #[codec(index = ...)] attributes, so neither depends on declaration order.

anchoring_invariants.receiver: must be the zero address, 32 zero bytes, with no Option marker and no length prefix

two_signature_domains.note: Because anchoring requires sender == receipt.executor, one key produces both signatures. They are still different signatures, because the messages differ.

json_wire.note: The serialized_transaction block reproduces current runtime serde output. It is interoperability evidence, not a new protocol rule.
json_wire.byte_representation: Hex strings appear exactly where a custom serializer exists: Address has its own impl Serialize, and the 64-byte signatures use serde_arr64. Plain [u8; 32] and Vec<u8> carry no annotation and fall through to serde's default sequence handling, so they emit arrays of numbers.
json_wire.tx_type: a plain string, the variant name
json_wire.payload: externally tagged: an object with the variant name as its single key

test_key.warning: TEST ONLY. NOT A PRODUCTION KEY. The seed is public.
test_key.source: resolved from test-vectors/receipt/receipt-v1.json; not restated here

valid.name: canonical-diagnostic-nonce
valid.note: The reference vector. The nonce is deliberately non-palindromic so a big-endian or compact encoding cannot produce the same signature.

valid.name: nonce-zero
valid.note: The realistic first-anchor case. Its all-zero nonce bytes cannot prove byte order, which is why the canonical vector exists; it guards against a consumer hard-coding the diagnostic nonce.

encoding_only.name: nonzero-amount-u128
encoding_only.note: NOT a valid AnchorReceipt. amount must be 0 for anchoring, so this case exists only to pin the fixed-width little-endian u128 encoding that a valid vector can never exercise. Do not submit it.
encoding_only.warning: ENCODING ONLY. This is not a consensus-valid AnchorReceipt transaction.
encoding_only.amount_note: Written as a decimal string, not a JSON number: the value exceeds the JavaScript safe-integer range, so a number literal would be silently rounded when parsed.

invalid.name: transaction-signature-over-receipt-hash
invalid.note: The transaction signature was produced over the raw 32-byte receipt hash, which is the receipt's message, not the transaction's. Everything else matches the canonical vector.

expected.why: Ed25519 is deterministic, so signing the receipt hash reproduces the receipt's own signature exactly. Reusing it as the transaction signature is the same mistake either way.

invalid.name: transaction-signature-over-prehashed-payload
invalid.note: The transaction signature was produced over BLAKE3 of the signing payload, applying the receipt's hash-then-sign pattern to a transaction. Transactions are signed over the raw payload with no prehash.

serialized_transaction.note: The exact serde JSON object for the canonical vector. The JSON-RPC envelope (jsonrpc, id, method, params) is deliberately not pinned here — the SDK wire tests already own it.
